messages:
Elena R: Hi team  first day! Enrolled my company Mac (M2 MBP) into Jamf but when I try to turn on FileVault it says 'FileVault recovery key not escrowed' and refuses to finish enabling. I followed the setup guide but stopped at the Apple ID screen. Any tips?

Riley (IT): welcome @Elena R :wave: We normally escrow the recovery key to Jamf so IT can rotate/recover if needed. On M1/M2 Macs FileVault requires a SecureToken user. Did you enroll using the Setup Assistant account we gave you or did you create a different local account?

Elena R: I used the account created during Setup Assistant. I didn't create another local user. The UI shows my account as "Enabled for FileVault: No".

Riley (IT): ok. Two quick things: 1) run `sudo fdesetup status` and paste output. 2) Can you run `dsmemberutil checkmembership -U $(whoami) -G admin` to confirm if your user is admin/has SecureToken.

Elena R: pasted outputs: ```$ sudo fdesetup status
FileVault is Off.

$ dsmemberutil checkmembership -U elenar -G admin
user is not a member of the group
```

Riley (IT): looks like the Setup Assistant left you as a standard user (weird but it happens). FileVault needs an admin with SecureToken to enable and escrow the key. I can do one of two things: 1) promote your account to admin and grant SecureToken via Jamf (short-lived admin) or 2) create an admin temporary user that has SecureToken, enable FileVault, escrow the key, then remove the temp user. Which do you prefer?

Jordan (People Ops): tagging IT policy: short-lived admin is fine for onboarding, but IT please log start/end times. Elena if you prefer not to have extra accounts we can do the admin-swap approach.

Elena R: Id rather avoid extra accounts. Temporary admin on mine for 30 mins is fine.

Ben (Security): FYI Security prefers the escrow option (we always escrow keys). Also we'll prompt you to create an optional personal recovery passphrase if you want.

Riley (IT): got it. Elena, can you paste the hardware UUID (About This Mac -> System Report -> Hardware UUID) or run `system_profiler SPHardwareDataType | grep UUID`? I'll target the Jamf policy.

Elena R: UUID: aaabbbb-cccc-1111-2222-333344445555 (pasted).

Jamf Bot: Policy "Grant temp admin & Escrow FileVault key" queued for device aaabbbb-cccc-1111-2222-333344445555. Estimated completion: ~4 minutes.

Riley (IT): pushing now. This will elevate your account, enable SecureToken for your user, enable FileVault and escrow the recovery key to Jamf Pro. Please save any work and keep the lid open for a prompt.

Elena R: Jamf notified me, I see a small approval toast. Running the enable flow now.

Jamf Bot: Policy "Enable FileVault & Escrow Key" completed for device aaabbbb-cccc-1111-2222-333344445555. Status: Success.

Riley (IT): ok you should be an admin now and FileVault turned on. Can you run `sudo fdesetup status` again and confirm? Also check System Preferences -> Security & Privacy -> FileVault shows "On" and says recovery key escrowed.

Elena R: `sudo fdesetup status` now returns `FileVault is On.` System Preferences shows FileVault: On and "Recovery key escrowed by your organization". All good.

Ben (Security): Nice. Elena, if you ever see "Personal recovery key" vs "Escrowed" open a ticket, do not post keys here.

Jordan (People Ops): welcome aboard Elena! If you need any onboarding help feel free to DM. Also heads up: we normally remove the temp admin role after a 24-hour window; Riley will confirm when it's removed.

Riley (IT): I'll drop a note here when the elevation is revoked. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

Elena R: thank you all  feeling set up now :smile:
